_doc: Per-edition decisions for usj_source.py's opt-in bracket/paren text-stripping. DEFAULT IS NO STRIPPING — an edition not listed here (or with a field omitted) gets its raw verse text, brackets and parens included, exactly as ingested; nothing is ever removed automatically. A rule should only be added here after a human has reviewed that edition's entry in config/text_strip_report.md (generated by `pipeline/scripts/text_strip_candidates.py`, or `make text-strip-report`) and is confident the flagged spans are genuine editorial/apparatus noise, not real translated or supplied content. Keyed by the edition tag as it appears in the ingest-cache dir name (pipeline/work/ingest-cache/usj-<tag>/...). Fields: strip_brackets (bool) — blanket-remove every [...] span; only sane when an edition uses [...] consistently for ONE purpose (e.g. long-form editorial commentary). Do NOT set this for an edition that uses [...] for supplied/added words (e.g. Young's Literal Translation-style editions) — that bracketed text is real translation content, not a note. strip_parens_noise (bool) — run usj_source._paren_is_noise's discriminating classifier over (...) spans (source-language citations, verse/book cross-references, 'ordagrant'/'betyder' metalinguistic glosses, f.Kr./e.Kr. era annotations) and drop only spans matching one of those patterns; everything else in parens is kept as real content (short alternate/amplified glosses are legitimate per docs/publishing-principles.md #4, not noise). reason (string, required alongside either flag) — the evidence that justified the decision, so a later reviewer doesn't have to re-derive it. strip_alternate_brackets / strip_alternate_parens (bool) — added 2026-09-30. Per-SPAN, not per-kind: drop a [...] or (...) span only when at least half of its content words (4+ letters; 2+ for CJK/Indic) also occur in the rest of the SAME verse outside every span, i.e. the span is a second rendering of the verse (an 'alternate'); spans with fewer than 2 content words, and spans that do not repeat their verse, are kept. Decided by usj_source.alternate_spans on the verse's whole text. The per-kind evidence is the `alternate` role in config/text_strip_report.md (pipeline/lexeme_aligner/span_roles.py). Independent of strip_brackets / strip_parens_noise and can be combined with them.

swk.reason: Svenska Kärnbibeln ('en expanderad översättning'). [...] is used exclusively for long-form editorial/study-note commentary inline in verse text — full-corpus sample: avg 18.7 words/span, up to 894 words in one span, often longer than the verse's own translated sentence; left unstripped this floods eflomal/gloss with non-scripture prose (measured: swk gap-fill precision collapsed to ~0.5-0.7% before this was found). (...) is a heterogeneous mix in the SAME edition: ~83% are short (one to a few words) alternate/amplified Swedish glosses that are genuine translated content worth aligning (e.g. '(blygdes)', '(oförtjänt kärlek, god favör)'), ~17% are real noise — source-language citations ('hebr. chesed', 'gr. logos'), cross-references ('1 Mos 1:1', 'vers 17'), metalinguistic glosses ('ordagrant ...', '... betyder ...'), era/date annotations ('735-715 f.Kr.'). Verified via full-corpus sweep across all 182 cached editions (the noise-pattern regexes are Swedish-lexical, checked they don't misfire on other languages' legitimate parenthetical scripture text) plus a controlled before/after benchmark A/B (git stash isolating the code change as the only variable): discriminating paren strip alone gave a small, consistent, non-regressive improvement (eflomal-Hebrew 67.6%->68.2%, gloss-Greek 75.2%->75.8%).

swe_svk.reason: 2026-09-10: discovered this rule had NEVER applied to the actual published Kärnbibeln edition — it was keyed only to `swk`, a separate benchmark-only ingest-cache tag (config/gold_langs.json's frozen gold-scoring reference) with byte-identical text to the production `swe_svk` tag (verified: the two ingest-cache USJ files compare equal). Every real onboarding/publish of Swedish ran with this edition's commentary brackets UNSTRIPPED the entire time. Same edition, same evidence, same rule — see the `swk` entry above for the full measurement. A client's downstream cross-referencing tool surfaced this independently: most of a 24-note Joshua test set they sent back were tagged SWALLOWED_ELSEWHERE/SELF_GLOSS — our alignment DID produce a span, but it landed inside a bracketed commentary block, exactly the failure mode this rule exists to prevent.

engwmv.reason: 2026-09-30, text-strip report v2 (span_roles 'alternate'): 76% of engwmv's parenthesised spans (24,331 evaluable, 42.4% of the edition's words) and 76% of its bracketed spans (1,525 evaluable) repeat at least half of their content words from elsewhere in the same verse — the parentheses are a running paraphrase of each clause ('(In the beginning God made out of nothing the heavens and the earth.)'), the brackets are 'or ...' variant renderings. 33.2% of the edition's words sit in repeating parens, 0.84% in repeating brackets; left in, every verse is counted twice and the repeated words compete for the same source tokens. Per-span, so the short non-repeating clarifications ('so', 'up') stay. Owner decision 2026-09-30.

urbpkf.reason: 2026-09-30, text-strip report v2 (span_roles 'alternate'): 51% of urbpkf's parenthesised spans (1,636 evaluable, 5.7% of the edition's words, 2.6% in repeating spans) repeat at least half of their content words from elsewhere in the same verse. Only the parentheses are listed: its brackets are not alternates (15% repetition, 0.04% of words). Per-span, so non-repeating parenthetical clauses are kept. Owner decision 2026-09-30 to strip without a prior read of the samples; the rule is narrow (repetition only) for that reason.
